name: Xteink X4
description: 4.26 inch monochrome ePaper e-reader, ESP32-C3, 800x480 panel mounted portrait (480x800 presentation). Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API when running CrossInk firmware with Tesserae client support: the dashboard is painted as the reader's sleep screen on an explicit sleep transition, so the radio never comes up on a timer. Server-side pack via esp32_bw_bin produces a raw 1-bpp mono buffer (48000 bytes) that is byte-identical to the firmware's framebuffer and is painted with no on-device decode.
notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware (GDEQ0426T82 / SSD1677) running CrossInk 1.4.0 with Tesserae client support. A frame composed at 480x800 portrait, packed at the 800x480 native stride, renders upright and correctly oriented on the panel.

Wire format is exactly 48000 bytes (800*480/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum, identical to seeed_reterminal_e1001 and xiao_epaper_75.

`portrait_flipped` is required, not cosmetic. The firmware paints the raw buffer straight into its framebuffer, whose scan origin is 180 degrees from the renderer's default; a plain `portrait` value renders the dashboard upside-down. This was first isolated by registering the same unit against the landscape `xiao_epaper_75` kind, which applies no rotation at all and still painted 180 degrees out, then confirmed with this entry in place.

Xteink shipped a second panel revision mid-production (SSD1677 -> UC8179). The firmware detects the controller at boot and both revisions consume the same buffer, so no separate SKU is needed.

See `xteink_x4_gray` for the 4-level grayscale variant of the same panel.
